title: Elastic Overrun Absorber and Prorated Invoice Mitigation
creator: Diego Martinez
description:
Goal: implement a resilient 'overrun absorber' mechanism that: 1) allows short-lived burst use of Dedicated pools via a controlled temporary boost, 2) records and attributes overrun consumption in a way that produces clear, prorated invoicing line-items, and 3) prevents accidental cost explosions through automatic dampening and tenant-level caps.

Context: Customers on Dedicated occasionally exceed their reserved throughput during traffic spikes. Current behavior allows temporary use of spare capacity (surge pools) but the billing signal is opaque and can lead to unexpected invoices. This ticket designs an engineering path to (a) surface a predictable temporary boost with explicit token/throughput accounting, (b) limit scope and duration via policy-driven dampeners, and (c) generate prorated invoice artifacts (line-item granularity per boost window).

Scope (this ticket):
- Implement the 'Overrun Absorber' controller in the fleet manager: a small stateful service that leases surge tokens against configured tenant allowances and emits audit events.
- Extend autoscaler policy DSL to support: boost_window_seconds, max_boost_rate, decay_backoff, and soft_cap_percent.
- Add metering hooks to the billing pipeline that tag tokens consumed during a boost window with boost_id, boost_rate, and prorated_multiplier.
- Provide operator metrics and a tenant-facing dashboard panel in Console for active boosts, historical boost windows, and estimated prorated charges.

Out of scope: complex UI billing disputes flows and legal invoice wording. This ticket will produce clear invoice line-items but not the final PDF/legal template (follow-up with finance).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Overrun Absorber can lease and release boost tokens per-tenant; 2) Autoscaler DSL accepts new boost policy fields and enforces max_boost_rate and boost_window_seconds; 3) Billing pipeline emits line-items with boost_id and prorated_multiplier visible in usage export; 4) Console shows real-time boost state and a historical chart for last 30 days; 5) SLOs: no regressions in p95 latency for dedicated inference under normal load.

notes:
Design trade-offs considered: 
- Option A (conservative): deny exceeding requests once tenant cap reached; easiest billing but poor customer UX.
- Option B (absorber): allow bursts but meter and prorate them; better UX but increases billing complexity.
We chose Option B to align with PLG goals but added strong dampening and operator visibility to limit risk.

Key implementation details:
- Boost windows are first-class objects: boost_id, tenant_id, start_ts, end_ts, max_rate, consumed_tokens.
- Prorated_multiplier formula: base_unit_price * (1 + alpha * (consumed_rate / reserved_rate)) where alpha is tunable per-tenant; default alpha=0.6.
- Decay_backoff: when a tenant uses boosts repeatedly, successive boost windows will have reduced max_rate for 24h to avoid hammering.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- Metrics: boost_windows_started, boost_windows_ended, boost_tokens_consumed_total, boost_prorate_multiplier_avg, boost_dropped_requests_due_to_hard_cap.
- Alerts: high continuous boost use (>3 windows in 24h), stuck boost_release not reconciled after 10m, billing tag pipeline lag >2m.

Migration: start with opt-in beta tenants. Enable a feature flag per-tenant in the control plane. Capture usage for 2 weeks in read-only (no charges) to validate multipliers and dashboard accuracy before billable rollout.
